title: GraniteBank - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
topics: dedicated GPU sizing and burst strategy
summary: Discovery focused on GraniteBank's need for dedicated GPU pools for latency-sensitive customer-facing features, strict network isolation and KMS integration. Discussed sizing (8-16 A100 equiv), burst policy, canary rollouts, and required security artifacts. Agreed next steps: send pricing, SOC2 & network diagrams, schedule 48-hour benchmark with sample prompts.
next_steps: Send Dedicated capacity pricing for 8/16 GPU configs and burst options
Share SOC2 report, network/VPC diagram, and KMS integration guide
Schedule 48hr benchmark window (setup by Redwood SE) for Jan 6-8
Follow up with legal for contract terms and data residency questions

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Elena (GraniteBank HoP), Tom (GraniteBank ML Eng), Aisha (GraniteBank CISO), Daniel (Granite Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Liam our SE. Quick intro and then we'd love to hear about your goals for dedicated capacity.
[00:12] Elena: Hi Maya, thanks. Quick intros from our side, I'm Elena, head of platform at GraniteBank. We run a mix of customer-facing chat features and internal document ingestion. Tom here runs the ML team, Aisha on security, Daniel on infra.
[00:25] Tom: Hey all.
[00:27] Liam: Hi team, quick one, are you leaning hosted first or do you expect private/on-prem?
[00:33] Elena: We're evaluating. Our primary need is isolation and predictable cost — can't have noisy neighbor spikes. So Dedicated looks like the right path, but we want to understand burst strategy and scaling.
[00:45] Aisha: And from security we need VPC peering, KMS, audit logs and retention controls. Also, data residency — some PII needs to stay in us-east-1.
[00:55] Maya: Totally. Today we support Dedicated with VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. Our Dedicated SKU gives reserved GPU pools with optional burst capacity to handle spikes.
[01:10] Daniel: When you say burst, is that overcommit or warm standby? How does it affect latency for in-flight requests?
[01:18] Liam: Good question. Our burst model is configurable: you can define a guaranteed baseline pool and an on-demand burst pool backed by spare capacity in the region. For strict latency SLOs we recommend a small warm standby so KV caches are primed; if you need absolute tail latency guarantees you can allocate extra reserved nodes. There's a tradeoff with cost.
[01:37] Tom: What about model variants? We do reranking and live chat. Some flows need a heavy 70B model, others can use a quantized 13B. How does routing and model fallback work?
[01:48] Liam: We support smart routing — policy based. You can route by latency vs cost: high-priority traffic hits the low-latency reserved pool with the larger model; fallback can go to a compatible quantized variant on the burst pool. We'll show you the routing policy we used for a fintech customer — it's in the deck we shared.
[02:05] Elena: Speaking of the deck, we saw the benchmarks but need to run with our prompts.
[02:10] Maya: Absolutely. We usually run a 48-hour benchmark with your prompt set and traffic profile. Liam will provision a dedicated pool for the run; we can pin the same kernel/quantization settings you plan to use in production.
[02:21] Aisha: On encryption, KMS integration, do you allow customer-managed keys in the private deployment or hosted?
[02:27] Liam: For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest model artifacts and logs; for Private (VPC or on-prem) you keep the keys fully customer side. Hosted API has envelope KMS options. We'll share our KMS integration guide.
[02:39] Daniel: Network wise, do you require a dedicated NAT or do we peer? What's the egress model?
[02:44] Maya: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-style setup; egress is through your AWS account when in VPC mode. We'll pass a network diagram for the peering and subnets.
[02:53] Tom: Latency expectations — our product team wants P95 < 350ms for short chat turns (<= 256 tokens). Can Dedicated achieve that?
[03:02] Liam: For short-turn workloads and 8xA100-equivalent reserved pool with continuous batching tuned for 256 tokens, P95 in the 200-300ms range is achievable. It depends on batching config, model size, and sequence length distribution. If you need headroom, we suggest 12-16 GPUs.
[03:18] Elena: Cost ballpark for 8 vs 16 GPUs? Also how billing works during burst usage?
[03:25] Maya: I'll send a pricing sheet, but rough: reserved monthly commit + a per-hour burst rate. Burst is billed on usage; if you exceed reserved capacity we route to burst pool and bill delta. There's also a sizing delta for standby nodes if you want primed caches.
[03:39] Aisha: Compliance — do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation and can we get audit logs with immutability?
[03:45] Maya: Yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. Audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or SIEM and we support append-only retention via your bucket policies. We'll share certs and the SOC2 report under NDA.
[03:58] Daniel: What about canary rollouts and model versioning? We need safe rollouts across prod traffic.
[04:04] Liam: We support canary and A/B rollouts at the route level with automatic rollback if latency or quality regressions are detected. You can pin routes to model versions and quant profiles.
[04:16] Tom: Any gotchas with KV cache warmup and cold starts? We do a lot of multi-turn chat where KV cache hits matter.
[04:23] Liam: Cold starts matter for KV caches. Warm standby nodes keep KV primed; otherwise first requests pay cache warm cost. For multi-turn we recommend session affinity and standby capacity. Our Optimize toolkit also suggests caching config based on your workload.
[04:38] Elena: About scaling — auto-scaling policies, are they reactive or scheduled? How fast do you scale?
[04:44] Liam: Autoscale is both: scheduled for predictable patterns and reactive for unexpected spikes. We offer scaling policy hooks (scale based on queue length, CPU/GPU utilization, or latency SLO breaches). Typical scale-out times are a few minutes, but if you need sub-30s tail guarantees we recommend hybrid reserved+warm standby.
[05:01] Aisha: For the benchmark run, can we isolate traffic and disable external internet access? We need to ensure data doesn't leave our VPC during tests.
[05:08] Maya: Yes, benchmark can run in your VPC with peering and no public egress. We'll coordinate network changes.
[05:15] Tom: Good. Also we need to run a sample of our reranking pipeline — can you run a multi-stage pipeline (embed -> index -> rerank -> generate)?
[05:23] Liam: Yes, we can support pipelines; for heavy rerankers we sometimes host the retrieval layer in your infra and run the model inference in Dedicated. We can also co-locate the index. We'll note that for the benchmark.
[05:34] Elena: Timeline: we'd like to run a POC before budget cycle in mid-Jan. Is that feasible?
[05:40] Maya: Yes. If we get sample prompts and traffic profile this week, we can schedule benchmark early Jan and have results before your review.
[05:47] Daniel: Any limitations on preferred hardware? We need to confirm GPU vendor and driver versions for compatibility with our internal tooling.
[05:54] Liam: We publish the instance types; Dedicated can be provisioned on A100/NVIDIA H100 equiv in most regions. We'll share driver/kernel lists. If you need specific kernel patches we can coordinate.
[06:05] Aisha: Legal — data residency and contract terms, we may need a data processing addendum.
[06:09] Maya: We have an enterprise DPA template and regional residency options. We'll loop in legal after we send the SOC2 and network docs.
[06:15] Elena: Ok recap and next steps?
[06:18] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send pricing for 8/16 GPU reserved configs and burst options, SOC2/ISO artifacts, VPC/network diagram, KMS guide, and benchmark plan. GraniteBank to share prompts, traffic profile, and regulatory checklist. We'll schedule the 48hr benchmark for Jan 6-8 pending availability.
[06:34] Tom: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:36] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up by EOD Friday with the docs and pricing.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present — e.g., "KV" sometimes transcribed as "K-V"; "H100" transcribed as "H-one-hundred" in snippets.
